title: Gisborne & East Cape August
meta_desc: Plan a family holiday in Gisborne & East Cape this August. Find out what's on, weather, crowd levels and tips for a fun and memorable trip with kids.
intro: Gisborne and the East Cape are perfect for a family holiday in August, with mild winter weather and plenty of outdoor activities to enjoy. The region offers a mix of surf beaches, scenic drives, and cultural experiences that cater to all ages. With a daily budget of $120-200 for a family of four, you can have a fun and memorable trip.

sections.heading: Weather in August
sections.body:
Gisborne and the East Cape experience mild winters, with average high temperatures ranging from 12-15°C (54-59°F) in August. It's a great time to enjoy outdoor activities like surfing, fishing, and exploring the scenic coastline.

Be sure to pack warm clothing, including jackets, hats, and gloves, as it can get chilly in the mornings and evenings. Rainfall is moderate, with an average of 12 rainy days throughout the month.

sections.heading: What's On in August
sections.body:
August is a great time to visit Gisborne and the East Cape, with various events and festivals taking place throughout the region. Some of the top events include the Gisborne Winter Festival, which features live music, food, and craft stalls.

The East Cape also hosts the annual East Cape Arts Festival, showcasing local art, music, and performances.

sections.heading: Best Activities for August
sections.body:
August is an excellent time to enjoy outdoor activities in Gisborne and the East Cape. Some of the top activities include surfing lessons at Wainui Beach, which offer beginner-friendly classes for kids and adults.

Visiting the East Cape Lighthouse, the easternmost point of New Zealand, is also a must-do, with stunning views of the coastline and surrounding landscape.
list: Surfing lessons at Wainui Beach ($60-$80 per person)
Visiting the East Cape Lighthouse (free admission)

sections.heading: Crowd Levels and Booking Ahead
sections.body:
August is considered the low season in Gisborne and the East Cape, with smaller crowds and a more relaxed atmosphere. However, it's still essential to book ahead for popular activities and accommodations, especially during school holidays.

Be sure to book your surfing lessons, accommodation, and any guided tours in advance to avoid disappointment.
list: Book surfing lessons at least 2 weeks in advance
Book accommodation at least 1 month in advance

sections.heading: Practical Tips for Families
sections.body:
When visiting Gisborne and the East Cape with kids, it's essential to be prepared for the outdoors. Pack warm clothing, including jackets, hats, and gloves, as well as sunscreen, sunglasses, and a first-aid kit.

Don't forget to bring a boogie board or bodyboard to enjoy the Rere Rockslide, a natural rock water slide in the river.
list: Bring a boogie board or bodyboard for the Rere Rockslide
Download the Gisborne and East Cape tourism app for maps and guides
Check the weather forecast before heading out each day
Bring a portable charger for your phone or camera
